clue.text: Pet — one of cat-lover's hates, primarily?

definitions.text: Pet — one of cat-lover's hates, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first, or primary, letter of each of the five words that come before it

explanation.surface: A dog is the sort of pet a cat devotee can't stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the initials spell a dog, a pet that a cat-lover may well dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooch is an informal word for a dog, the classic pet that cat enthusiasts are supposed to dislike.

clue.text: Probes succeeded, set up for female cleric

parts.note: pries means probes or snoops

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the two words before it are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
taken as written

explanation.surface: Investigations went well and were arranged for a woman of the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who performs sacred rites in a temple or church is a female member of the clergy.

clue.text: Surgery on muscular spasm affecting vision?

parts.note: an op is a surgical operation
a tic is an involuntary muscular twitch

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an operation on a twitching muscle might harm someone's eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an adjective relating to the eye or sight, so it describes something to do with seeing.

clue.text: Nasty cavity around radius bone

indicators.note: around says the word for cavity goes either side of the other two pieces

parts.note: a hole is a cavity
R is the abbreviation for radius in geometry
a rib is a bone of the chest

explanation.surface: An unpleasant hollow next to the radius, a bone of the forearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radius' and 'bone' read as anatomy together, but they give R and RIB separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrible and nasty are close synonyms for something very unpleasant.

clue.text: Good impression which one should look for before signing

definitions.text: which one should look for before signing

parts.note: fine means good, as in a fine effort
a print is an impression made by pressing, like a fingerprint

explanation.surface: Advice to read a contract carefully before putting your name to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-type terms and conditions in a contract are what a careful signer checks before committing.

clue.text: Bug multiplied by constant changing

parts.note: a bug is informally a virus such as flu
X is the multiplication sign

explanation.surface: A germ spreading fast, multiplying continually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constant' looks like a maths term beside 'multiplied by', but it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Flux is a state of continuous change, as in a situation in flux.

clue.text: Reassuring remark today containing too much apology (not the first)

indicators.note: containing says the word for today holds the abbreviation for excessive

parts.note: now means at the present day

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter of the apology is dropped

parts.note: sorry is the usual apology

explanation.surface: Someone today offering an over-the-top apology that turns out to be reassurance.
explanation.definitionFit: A common British phrase said to put someone's mind at rest, a comforting word of reassurance.

clue.text: Significant body with direction influenced by Sun?

definitions.text: Significant body with direction influenced by Sun?

parts.words: Significant body with direction influenced by Sun
parts.note: a large heavenly body whose path through space is governed by the star at the centre of our system; Sun in italics also suggests the British tabloid

explanation.surface: An important organisation whose editorial line is shaped by The Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic 'Sun' suggests the British tabloid newspaper and 'body' an organisation; read literally it is a world in orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A large celestial body such as Mars, whose orbit around the star is controlled by solar gravity.

clue.text: Grass up with malice and tip off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of kilter, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An informer spitefully betrays someone and alerts the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass up' is British slang for informing on someone; 'off' rearranges MALICE with TIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass someone up is to inform on them, and to implicate is to show someone is involved in a crime.

clue.text: Judge to serve on tribunal, maybe missing one private meeting

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it

indicators.note: missing says the letter for one is left out

parts.note: to sit is to serve as a member of a court or tribunal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A judge preparing to serve on a tribunal but one member short.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret meeting, especially between lovers, so a private rendezvous.

clue.text: Butt in middle of ashtray after burning slip gets put out

indicators.note: after places the centre of the ashtray behind the word for burning

parts.note: a fire that is still in is still burning

indicators.note: middle of picks out the central letter of the seven-letter word ashtray

parts.note: to err is to slip up or make a mistake

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of put are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A cigarette end left in an ashtray after a slip-up is extinguished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' looks like a cigarette end, but 'Butt in' is the definition. IN is the old sense of burning, as in 'is the fire still in?'; 'out' turns PUT into UPT.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt in is to break into a conversation uninvited, a synonym for cutting someone off mid-sentence.

clue.text: Use obvious description for cider?

definitions.meaning: to use something is to put it into practice, as in putting a theory to work
cider is made from fruit off the orchard tree, so it might be called fruity in the style of 'apple-ish'

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek instruction to describe cider in the plainest terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a whimsical coinage: something tasting of apples is 'apple-y', spelt like the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To use a method or rule is to put it to work; and cider, made from apples, could jokingly be called apple-flavoured.

clue.text: Criticism when taking time out: that is ill-deserved leave?

indicators.note: out says the letter for time is taken away from the word for criticism

parts.note: stick is informal for criticism, as in giving someone stick
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A grumble that someone's time off work was undeserved.
explanation.walkthrough: A sickie is British slang for a day off work claimed as sick leave when not really ill; 'ill-deserved' hints at both the pretended illness and the undeserved break.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British term for a day's absence taken by pretending to be unwell, so leave that the feigned illness does not earn.

clue.text: Mailer possibly coming from cat catalogue after half a month

indicators.note: after places the word for catalogue behind the half-month

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mailer' poses as someone who posts things; it is Norman Mailer, the American author of The Naked and the Dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Mailer was an American writer of fiction, so he is an example of an author of books.

clue.text: Method of blending in fine, in mashed guacamole

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.walkthrough: 'blending' and 'mashed' suggest cooking, but the definition means hiding by merging with surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Disguise by colouring or covering that lets something merge with its surroundings, a technique for going unseen.

clue.text: Home for many Latinos scattered over Dallas

explanation.surface: Latino families spread around the Texas city of Dallas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges OVER and DALLAS together into the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American country whose people are largely Spanish-speaking Latin Americans, so it is home to many of them.

clue.text: Baggy article of Dior's in copies with belt up on top

clue.text: Severely damage ability to hit on mark

clue.text: What could be seated in place, under …

explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs into the next clue: the base goes under the figure clued at 21 down.

clue.text: Graceful bird's tail changes to black mop

clue.text: Rude nature of rows seen developing in Civil Service

clue.text: Occasional excuse for deploying a chocolate soldier?
